title: introduce-prefill-heat-station-tenant-cost-differentiator
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Several tenants with diverse traffic patterns were getting suboptimal default prefill, batching, and quantization settings. Small tenants with bursty traffic were over-provisioned (higher token cost), while large low-latency tenants were under-utilizing prefill capabilities. This PR introduces a telemetry-driven "heat station" that synthesizes tenant heat signatures from prefix reuse, arrival skews, and burstiness, and uses that signal to automatically apply a recommended tenant-level defaults bundle (batching, cache horizon, quantization preset, and cost guardrails).

What this PR changes (high level): Adds a lightweight prefilling policy composer and a new tenant defaults catalog. The composer runs in the control plane and emits tenant-defaults objects that the serving runtime and autoscaler can consume. For retro-compatibility the system falls back to existing tenant defaults when telemetry is sparse. Key features: 1) heat-station collector: summarizer of prefix reuse, inter-arrival variance, and KV-cache hit rates; 2) default bundles: curated combos of batch shapes, cache horizons, and quant presets (cpu/gpu friendly); 3) unit-econ estimator: simulated per-tenant token cost and latency profile for validating recommendations; 4) conservative rollout: canary rollout to 5% of tenants with dark traffic simulations and rollback hooks.

Implementation notes: The implementation is split into three areas: control plane (prefill/composer service), runtime adapters (APIs for applying tenant defaults), and CLI/telemetry. The prefilling composer is implemented as a new microservice (prefill-heatstation) with an HTTP API and gRPC push to configstore. It pulls aggregated telemetry from the existing telemetry-aggregator endpoint and runs a lightweight rules engine to map heat signatures to bundles. Bundles are defined as YAML presets in catalog/prefill_bundles/*.yaml and validated with unit-econ tests. The runtime adapter accepts tenant-defaults via ConfigStore and exposes a short TTL for dynamic updates to avoid flapping.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for the rules engine and catalog validation added, integration test that simulates three tenant archetypes (steady low-rate, bursty microbursts, steady high-throughput) verifying recommended bundles reduce per-token cost by 7-22% in simulation while keeping P95 latency within SLO. E2E smoke tests added to the CICD pipeline to verify the gRPC contract between composer and configstore. Telemetry retention for the heat-station is conservative (14 days) to protect privacy and reduce noise.

Rollout plan: Step 1: deploy prefill-heatstation to staging telemetry and collect 48h of signatures. Step 2: dry-run mode in production where recommendations are written to audit-only namespace for 72h. Step 3: canary apply to 5% of tenants with automatic rollback on unit-econ regressions (>5% cost increase) or latency SLO violations. Step 4: advertise in Console with opt-out toggle per tenant and revert path.

Checklist:
- [x] heat-station service + basic rules engine
- [x] catalog of 6 initial bundles (balanced, latency-opt, thrift, burst-friendly, microburst, conservative)
- [x] unit-econ estimator and simulation harness
- [x] runtime adapter and configstore integration
- [x] CI integration tests and docs in design/prefill-heatstation.md
- [x] console toggle and audit-only namespace

Related: builds on ENG-2159 (tenant-defaults-unification) and ENG-2201 (telemetry-aggregator-sharding). Also referenced in SUP-1342 customer request to reduce costs for low-volume bursty tenants.

Notes on safety: All recommendations are conservative by default and require explicit enable or canary opt-in. Quant presets include a stringency level; aggressive quant presets are gated behind tenant opt-in and tenant-level policy.

Migrations: Adds catalog YAMLs and a new DB table prefills. Prefill recommendations are idempotent objects keyed by tenant_id and composer_version. Backwards compatibility preserved; if ConfigStore doesn't receive a prefills object the runtime continues using legacy defaults.

Metrics to watch post-merge: per-tenant unit cost (tokens/USD), P95 latency, cache hit rate, rollback triggers, and percent of tenants accepting recommendations.

review_comments: Noah Patel: Please add unit tests for the conservative->aggressive quant transition path (hotpath). Missing tests could allow an aggressive quant preset to leak into canary tenants.
Ava Martinez: Added unit tests for transition path and tightened rules engine thresholds. Also added a test harness case that exercises quant gating.
Sofia Chen: Runtime adapter should expose a metric for 'applied_recommendation_version' to help troubleshooting during rollout. Also suggest a backoff when configstore returns transient failures.
Ava Martinez: Instrumented applied_recommendation_version and added exponential backoff with jitter to the adapter. Added a note to design doc about backoff choices.
Marcus Green: CI e2e flakes on a test verifying gRPC contract — looks like test timeout. Increase timeout and assert on schema rather than exact sequence of events.
Ava Martinez: Increased timeout and updated assertion. Reran CI; e2e stabilized.
Sofia Chen: Approved pending docs for 'how to opt out' in Console and a sample rollback runbook.
Ava Martinez: Added opt-out docs and rollback runbook to design/prefill-heatstation.md. Marking as ready for merge.
merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2026-02-18 by maintainer (squash-merge). No conflicts. Changelog entry added under releases/2026-02.md
release_notes: Introduces the Prefill Heat Station: telemetry-driven tenant default composer that recommends batching, cache horizon, and quant presets per tenant heat signature. Initial rollout will be audit-only and canary-enabled. Expected per-tenant cost reductions for certain archetypes (7-22% in simulation).
notes_for_ops: Deploy notes in design/prefill-heatstation.md. Default rollout is disabled; to enable for a tenant add annotation 'prefill.heatstation/enabled=true' in tenant metadata. Monitor 'prefill.recommendation.applied' and unit-econ delta metric. If regressions observed, flip 'prefill.heatstation/rollback' flag for the tenant which will force revert to legacy defaults.
